title: RCMP Arrests Five in Extortion Probe Targeting British Columbia Car Dealership
excerpt: The coordinated arrests followed a year-long RCMP investigation, Project E_PURSUANCE, into extortion demands, arson and shootings targeting an auto dealership's co-owners in Surrey and Langley.
body:
• Five men were arrested Thursday — four in Surrey, B.C., and one at Toronto's Pearson Airport — after a year-long RCMP probe, Project E_PURSUANCE, into extortion against the co-owners of an auto dealership.
  • The dealership reported extreme extortion demands in June 2025, followed by targeted arson and shootings at its Surrey and Langley locations.
  • Charges include extortion, multiple firearms counts, explosives, property damage and drug trafficking; police seized firearms, ammunition and suspected drugs including cocaine, fentanyl and opium.
  • All five remain in custody with bail hearings scheduled for October 5 in Surrey; RCMP says additional suspects have been identified and more charges are expected.

Year-long RCMP investigation ends in coordinated arrests

Five foreign nationals were arrested and charged on Thursday after the co-owners of an auto dealership reported extortion attempts and two targeted attacks involving arson and shootings at their Surrey and Langley locations in British Columbia. Four of the men were arrested in Surrey; the fifth — 23-year-old Indian national Sanket Singla, who had been tracked while overseas — was arrested at Toronto's Pearson Airport, according to reports on the RCMP announcement.

https://x.com/VancouverSun/status/2106187528579514687

Singla has been charged with extortion, two firearm counts, property damage and an explosives charge. The other four arrested in Surrey are Simranjeet Singh, 24, charged with extortion, two firearm counts, property damage and an explosives charge; Jagdeep Singh, 24, from Ottawa, charged with extortion, a firearm count and property damage; a 24-year-old Surrey man charged with extortion, six firearm counts and two drug trafficking counts; and a 21-year-old Surrey man charged with extortion, two firearm counts and property damage. Police did not provide the full names of the latter two. All five remain in custody pending bail hearings on October 5 in Surrey.

Context & Background

The RCMP investigation, dubbed Project E_PURSUANCE, began in June 2025 after the dealership's co-owners reported what police described as extreme extortion demands. The demands were followed by shootings and arson at the dealership's Langley and Surrey locations. During the coordinated arrests, police seized firearms, ammunition, magazines and suspected drugs.

The case is part of a wider pattern of extortion reported in several Canadian cities with large South Asian populations. In September, Calgary police released photographs of 15 Indian-origin men charged in connection with a separate series of extortion cases, linking the investigation to 49 reported incidents including 19 shootings, and said most of the accused were Indian nationals living in Canada on student or work permits.

Diaspora Angle

The investigation targeted extortion against members of British Columbia's South Asian community — the same community now being urged to cooperate with police. RCMP Superintendent Harm Dosange said investigators repeatedly heard the same message from victims: "We came here. Our life's work. We've worked hard. Now people are trying to take that away from us." For the South Asian diaspora in Canada's Lower Mainland, the arrests mark the first major break in a wave of extortion that has strained trust within the community for over a year.

"The RCMP's position was we were going to target the higher levels of the extortion and hold them accountable."

— RCMP Supt. Harm Dosange

What's Next

The five accused face bail hearings in Surrey on October 5. RCMP says it has identified additional suspects, is sharing evidence with policing partners across Canada, and expects more charges — including potential extortion-related offences across Western Canada uncovered during the investigation. According to reports, any alleged ties to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang will be tested at trial. Authorities continue to ask members of the public, particularly in the South Asian community, to come forward with information.
